paragraphs: A pontoon boat is a deck on floats, and that is exactly why it succeeded. No hull shape to compromise around means the whole surface is usable, which turns the boat into a floating patio rather than something to be piloted.

The model holds 163,960 polygons and 178,206 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 21 maps, 16 at 4096x4096, 2 at 2048x2048 and 3 smaller. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $79 it suits leisure and marine visualisation, lakeside and marina scenes, tourism and advertising imagery, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2019.

Queen Alexandra's birdwing is the largest butterfly in the world, found in one small area of Papua New Guinea and protected everywhere. The female is bigger and plainer; the male carries the colour, and both are large enough that they were first collected with a shotgun.

The model holds 25,862 polygons and 25,783 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps all at 4096x4096, with fur and in a flying pose. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits wildlife and nature visualisation, museum and education work, conservation material, advertising, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

The Spacelander was a commercial failure and is now one of the most collectable bicycles ever made. A fibreglass body shaped like something from a comic strip, sold at a price nobody would pay in its own decade, and produced in numbers small enough to make survivors valuable.
The model holds 197,178 polygons and 209,856 vertices, built in quads only with overlapping UVs, in cream. It carries StemCell certification.
At $79 it suits design and product visualisation, museum and exhibition work, period film and advertising, retro scenes, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Radio direction finding answers one question that nothing else can: where is the person transmitting. Air traffic and vessel traffic services rely on it precisely when everything else has failed, because a mayday call is sometimes the only signal a lost aircraft or boat can still produce.
The model holds 110,528 polygons and 116,079 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps all at 4096x4096, supplied with the antenna. It carries StemCell certification.
At $79 it suits aviation and maritime infrastructure visualisation, equipment marketing, control tower and station scenes, training material and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

A monster in a plant pot is funny and threatening at the same time, which is why the idea keeps coming back. The pot domesticates it, the teeth do not, and the joke works because everyone knows what a houseplant is supposed to do.
The model is light at 40,014 polygons and 20,357 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to real time use. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits game creatures, animation and children's media, horror comedy and film props, concept art, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

The yellow school bus is a regulated colour, chosen decades ago because it is the most visible thing on a road at dawn. Everything else about the vehicle follows from carrying children who are not wearing belts: high seat backs, no sharp edges, and a body built to stay upright.
The model is supplied with a simple interior and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits urban and suburban visualisation, education and safety material, film and television, advertising, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

A rhino horn is not bone and not attached to the skull. It is keratin, the same material as hair and fingernails, growing from the skin, which is why it can be worn down and regrow, and why the trade that has nearly destroyed the animal is built on a misunderstanding.
The model holds 35,732 polygons and 35,821 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied as a head with fur. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $69 it suits wildlife and conservation visualisation, documentary and education work, museum material, close up illustration, advertising and game assets. On sale since 2021.

Amber glass exists because light destroys what is inside. It blocks the wavelengths that break down essential oils and medicines, which is why the colour became the visual shorthand for anything sold as natural, clinical or carefully made.
The set is very light at 10,057 polygons and 10,029 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, so it costs nothing in a product scene. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $69 it suits packaging and product visualisation, cosmetics and pharmaceutical presentation, e-commerce imagery, advertising, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

A tornado is not a shape, it is a process, which is why modelling one as geometry never convinces. Volumetric data is the honest way to do it: density that varies through the column, so the funnel can be lit and rendered as the moving air it actually is.
This is supplied as animated VDB volume data prepared for Blender, so it opens as a native scene rather than an import. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $69 it suits weather and disaster visualisation, documentary and news graphics, film and television effects, education material and game cinematics. On sale since 2026.

Conference audio is a discipline of its own. A microphone on a stem in front of every delegate, each one switchable, each one feeding a system that has to keep dozens of people intelligible in a room built of hard surfaces.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the devices and microphones as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $69 the set suits conference and interior visualisation, AV equipment marketing, corporate and institutional scenes, product imagery, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2026.

A bus driver's seat is suspended, air sprung and adjustable in more directions than a car seat, because the person in it is at work for hours on a vehicle with a stiff chassis. It is occupational health equipment that happens to look like furniture.
The model is very light at 11,730 polygons and 6,620 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, so it fits any interior build. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $69 it suits vehicle interior visualisation, transport and fleet presentation, equipment marketing, product imagery, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2023.

Capsule architecture treats a dwelling as a manufactured product rather than a building. Made in a factory, delivered whole, and plugged into services on arrival, it is an idea that has been reinvented in every decade since the sixties and never quite become normal.
The model holds 68,349 polygons and 73,673 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.

At $69 it suits architectural and modular housing visualisation, property and innovation presentation, landscape scenes, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Cinema cameras stopped looking like cameras once the body became a computer with a sensor in it. What is left is a box with mounting points, and the shape of any given rig is decided by whoever assembles it rather than by the manufacturer.
The model is light at 38,271 polygons and 40,825 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the indicator light on. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $69 it suits product and equipment visualisation, film production and studio scenes, e-commerce imagery, advertising, previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A push cart is a folding frame that has to survive being thrown in and out of a boot several hundred times a year, carry a bag heavier than a small child, and collapse to a size one person can lift. It is a mechanism problem disguised as a trolley.
The model holds 117,213 polygons and 117,779 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is enough for close product work. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $69 it suits sports equipment and retail visualisation, e-commerce imagery, advertising, golf course scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.
